items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Budd Johnson was with him at the time.

ctx.x: Earl Hines was a marvelous leader. I didn’t have an opportunity to work too much with Gates, except on a couple of occasions with a small group, after he had Marva [Josie], the singer, and Budd Johnson was with him at the time. But he was a nice man, a great musician. I’m very proud of the fact that he got Louis Armstrong involved in – with his playing, or Louis got him involved. They inspired each other. But
Louis played – Earl played what they call the trumpet-style on piano. He was a good musician.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I knew of him. I didn't know him personally.

ctx.x: Explain that if you can, Budd, because I think you and Clark Terry and Buster Bailey --
Clark was a master and Buster was a --
And Buster would be in there and Clark Kerry, one of the few people that know about this circular breathing.
